newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt softening people for less spending - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt softening people for less spending - Cullen.

text.p: Opposition finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Wednesday Finance Minister Bill Birch is softening the public up to break spending commitments made in the coalition agreement.
Cullen was commenting on Birch's comments that NZ$1.2 billion of extra spending agreed for 1997/98 had to be carefully costed "in a way that we weren't able to do during the negotiations".
Birch said the negotiations were taken "under a fair bit of necessity to get them concluded".
Cullen said Birch had joined a growing list of National Party Cabinet ministers who were attempting to undermine the agreement.
"National is preparing the ground now for a retreat from the promises to invest in health and education and other areas of neglect," Cullen said.
Cullen said that Birch's comment that fiscal policy had to be supportive of monetary policy was code for cutting public spending. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
